Paragraph: Sitting on the shores of the vast ocean, the Vanara search party was paralyzed by despair, believing they had failed their mission to find Sita. Seeing their loss of hope, the elder Jambavan approached Hanuman, reminding him of his latent divine strength: 'Why are you quiet, O valiant Hanuman? You possess matchless speed, wisdom, and power. Arise, remember your true self and leap across the ocean!'
Situation/Problem_Faced: Collective helplessness, low self-esteem, imposter syndrome, and paralysis of action when facing a seemingly impossible challenge.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Jambavan acts as a mentor, invoking Hanuman's forgotten strengths through positive reinforcement and cognitive reframing.
Outcome/Resolution: Hanuman awakens to his immense capabilities, sheds self-doubt, and expands in size to execute the legendary leap to Lanka.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Self-Esteem: Overcoming imposter syndrome, Unlocking latent confidence

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Atma-Smriti (Remembrance of one's innate divine potential)
Guru-Kripa / Mentor Guidance (The therapeutic role of an elder awakening self-worth)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Jambavan helps Hanuman remember his true, unbounded nature, proving that divine power often lies dormant within us waiting to be awakened.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: An example of strengths-based cognitive reframing that lifts individuals out of learned helplessness.
